notes: Recorded under the owner's AFK mandate, continuing through the ranked remainder. Item 5 listed mcp-re-transport as a wholly unowned crate. Recorded by the implementing agent as routine owner-review maintenance, not as a transcription of a ruling naming this fingerprint. A MEASUREMENT CORRECTION IS PART OF THIS SLICE. The first reading of this crate counted inline cfg(test) blocks and concluded it was an EVIDENCE gap, five of nine source files having none. That was wrong. The evidence lives in tests/ — five guards in mtls_client_test.rs, four bounds in dos_hardening_test.rs, twenty framing and header controls in the lib, and a fault-injection lane whose Bazel targets are explicitly NOT manual and therefore run on every bazel test //... It is an OWNERSHIP gap over evidence that already exists, like the keysources. The corrected measurement is what this registration rests on. TWO UNITS, because the crate holds two authorities: whom this client trusts to be the proxy is not the same question as what it is willing to read off the wire, and one unit answering both would need an 'and' in its answer to ADR-MCPRE-061 section 8 question 1. THE ASYMMETRY IS THE REASON THIS CLAIM IS WORTH STATING. Presenting a client certificate is visible when it is missing — the handshake fails loudly on the first connection. VERIFYING the server is not: an accept-any verifier completes every handshake, so a deployment with no server authentication at all looks exactly like a correct one. Every request succeeds, every response parses, and nothing in the transcript says the proxy on the other end was never authenticated. WHERE THE LOAD-BEARING DEMONSTRATION LIVES, AND WHY IT IS NOT A TESTED SYMBOL OF THIS UNIT. tests/fault_injection_test.rs compiles the crate with fault_accept_any_server, which DISCARDS the WebPkiServerVerifier and installs an accept-any verifier, then asserts that the very scenarios the guards reject are ACCEPTED — the untrusted server cert reaches the handler, and so does the wrong-identity one. That is a genuine catch demonstration, and its Bazel targets are explicitly not manual. It CANNOT be evidence of this unit, because it runs in a lane where the property this theorem states is deliberately false, and a unit citing both would name controls that cannot pass together. So it is named in the scope and cited nowhere. THE PROBE REACHES THE ONE CONJUNCT A WEAKENING CAN REACH IN THIS LANE — the empty-bundle refusal, M130, red-verified. The other three rest on rustls enforcing what WebPkiServerVerifier is documented to enforce, which is a property of that library and not of this code, and the scope says so rather than implying the probe covers them. WHAT IS NOT CLAIMED: nothing about what the proxy does once the handshake succeeds; nothing about the signing above this layer, since the crate is transport-only and does no signing; and nothing about the configured server CA being the RIGHT one, which is the operator's trust decision — this theorem is about honouring it, not about choosing it.
